correctness.rationale: Exact intrinsic width W=2 max_edges|X_i-X_j|/R with R²~χ²_(n-1) and radial independence. In Gaussian edge variables adjacent correlations have abs value 1/2; integrating bivariate Gaussian tail yields C u^-2 exp(-2u²/3), allowing dependency Poisson error O(Δ m^(-1/3)(log m)^(-1/3)) and thus Δ=o(m^(1/3)). Uniform bounded-degree matching gives double-exponential negative and exponential positive tails for normalized maxima, enough for second-moment convergence and path variance 2π²/3 via b_m²~4 log m and radial normalization. Fixed positive leaf fractions imply each hub leaf maximum and negative minimum differ by a_m by o_L2(1); finitely many core edges vanish after subtraction, so limit max|Z_j| and moments. Polar computation yields v1=v2=1-2/π, differing CDFs (2Φ(t)-1)^k. The finite core Gaussian integral follows by conditioning on hubs. These calculations are analytic not Monte Carlo extrapolation.
residual_risks: Moment tail inequalities require uniform constants in fixed Δ and core k; bounds given in RESULT.
New growing-degree hypothesis is sufficient, not known optimal.

value.rationale: Two distinct fluctuation scales for combinatorially identical tree crosspolytopes, sharp path variance and fixed multihub distribution/variance constants address a natural metric-geometric invariant. The k=2 variance coincidence despite different laws is a meaningful exact structural comparison; the enhanced degree window supplies a nontrivial quantitative probabilistic improvement.
residual_risks: Covered bounded-degree Gumbel and star consequences are not valued as new contributions.

final_claim: For intrinsic Euclidean symmetric-edge widths, Gumbel weak convergence holds for Δ=o(m^(1/3)); bounded-degree cases also have sharp scaled variance, including n log n Var(W_path)->2π²/3. For every fixed k-hub tree with positive leaf fractions, centered width converges with first two moments to max_{j<=k}|Z_j|, giving v1=v2=1-2/π but distinct limiting distributions.
limitations: Growing-degree hypothesis is only sufficient; moment convergence there is not proved.
All fixed hub proportions must remain strictly positive, k fixed, no intermediate hub-scale classification.
Scientific acceptance is for the genuinely additional combined results; published earlier covered subclaims must be acknowledged.
